title: Flying with Presentation Equipment: Ride and Venue Handoffs
description: Plan airport transportation with presentation equipment: check flight restrictions, confirm packed cases, venue access and the person receiving the kit.
cta: Confirm the passenger ride and equipment handoff before your event.
image_alt: A closed charcoal equipment case and an open cable pouch on a pale stone floor in a sunlit convention foyer.
body:
Before booking an airport ride with presentation equipment, decide which items will travel with you, confirm the complete passenger, luggage and equipment load, and get the venue's receiving instructions. Keep the flight, car pickup and venue handoff in one plan, with a named person responsible for the equipment at each stage.

A laptop bag for a meeting and several cases for an exhibition create different handoffs. The useful question is not simply which vehicle to request: it is whether the equipment can follow the same route and entrance as the traveler.

Prepare an equipment brief alongside the passenger details

List every packed case, display tube and bag, including personal luggage. Record outside dimensions, units and weight for the equipment cases. Flag fragile contents, items that must remain upright, and anything that needs special handling. Ask the transportation provider to confirm the actual arrangement rather than inferring fit from a vehicle class.

Our airport luggage planning guide covers the measurement brief. For presentation equipment, add who will load, unload and carry each case, and whether the traveler can manage the venue's permitted entrance. Confirm any assistance separately. Vans, Sprinters and buses require a quote.

Check the flight rules before packing the kit

Check your airline's current size, weight and equipment requirements for the actual itinerary. Separate the items you need to keep with you from anything accepted as checked baggage, and make that distinction clear to colleagues who help pack.

The FAA's lithium-battery guidance requires spare lithium batteries and power banks to travel in the cabin, with terminals protected against short circuit. Remove them if a carry-on bag is checked at the gate. Check battery ratings and the airline's own limits before travel; approval requirements and restrictions can differ by battery and carrier.

Do not assume that a case of batteries for giveaways or sale falls within the ordinary passenger allowance. The FAA's passenger battery resource distinguishes passenger-use batteries from stock for further sale or distribution. Resolve that question with the airline or an appropriate shipping specialist before bringing the kit to the airport.

Confirm the venue entrance and receiving arrangement

Ask the organizer for the building, entrance, event contact and access window. Establish whether your load qualifies for hand-carry, needs a loading dock, or must be handled through the event's freight contractor. A passenger drop-off address alone does not confirm equipment access or permission to unload.

For a San Francisco example, Moscone Center's freight-handling guidance limits lobby hand-carry to small items carried by hand in a single trip without freight-handling equipment. It prohibits carts and dollies in lobby areas and directs loading-dock coordination through the event's General Service Contractor. Get instructions for your particular event before setting the destination.

If the cases need a freight arrangement, organize that separately with the event team and agree where the presenter will be dropped off. Also confirm early receiving and storage before relying on them. Hotel luggage storage and event freight receiving are separate arrangements.

Name the person responsible at every handoff

  • At departure: one traveler checks the complete case list before leaving the office or hotel.
  • At airport pickup: collect all checked equipment, then follow the agreed pickup instructions. Tell the provider if a missing case is delaying readiness.
  • At the venue: identify who will receive the cases and where that person will meet the traveler.
  • After the event: confirm who repacks, where empty cases are kept and when they can be collected for the return ride.

Keep a simple numbered inventory that can be checked without exposing confidential contents. Confirm any high-value, fragile or specialist handling needs, along with the applicable equipment handling and coverage terms, with the relevant providers before booking.

Leave room between landing and the presentation

Work backward from the required technical check or rehearsal, not just the audience start time. Include leaving the aircraft, any entry formalities, baggage collection, reaching pickup, the drive, venue access and setup. Use current estimates for the travel date and allow a margin for disruption.

Example: a presenter travels with a backpack, a suitcase and two equipment cases. Before booking, the team sends the complete load to the ride provider, confirms the event's permitted handoff route, and names a colleague to receive the cases. The presenter keeps essential presentation files and adapters accessible. If the flight is delayed, the event contact checks an agreed fallback, such as previously arranged onsite equipment. This illustrates coordination, not a vehicle-fit or arrival-time guarantee.

A presentation-equipment handoff you can copy

Passenger and equipment transfer brief
Date, airport and flight: [details].
Travelers and personal bags: [complete counts].
Equipment: [numbered packed-case list, outside dimensions, units and weights].
Handling requirements: [fragile or upright items; who loads, unloads and carries them].
Venue: [building, confirmed entrance or separately arranged receiving point, access window].
Handoff: [reachable traveler and receiving contact].
Schedule: [technical check, event start and realistic delay margin].
Return: [case retrieval, repacking and any additional stop].
Please confirm the vehicle arrangement, pickup instructions, stops and applicable waiting or change terms.

Use this brief when arranging Koast airport transfers or corporate transportation. For a Bay Area conference, specify the airport and exact venue address, including any confirmed stop before the event. Keep the event's equipment receiving plan attached to the itinerary.
